call_points.text: Gross margin pressure is due to legacy orders (fixed price) and commodity inflation; price variation clauses are now mandatory in new contracts.
Export revenue is 10-12% of total, expected to grow with the Kolkata plant capex, providing a natural forex hedge.
All expansion programs (Baroda and Kolkata plants) are on track with staggered completion timelines.
FY26 orders grew 27.4%, sales 9.6% and profit before tax 10.1%.
Order backlog is around 50% higher than last year.
Q4 order intake was low because management was selective, booking only orders with price-variation clauses.
FY26 gross margin fell about 1.5-1.6%, with commodity costs accounting for almost 1%.
Q4 gross margin was hit by about 2.5% from commodity costs.
Q4 included a ₹14 Cr exceptional charge from Labour Code restructuring, versus an ₹18 Cr tax-litigation gain last year.
Data centres are 10-12% of the order backlog; management expects the share to rise.
New BESS offering launched; company makes the system but sources batteries from partners.
Commodity hedging covers 50-60%; forex hedged order-by-order and on net ARAP.
Analyst pressed on opaque data-centre answers; management declined to give an absolute percentage.
Management said it is not the cost leader in BESS but competes on quality and advisory software.

timeline.summary: Schneider Electric Infrastructure announced the merger of its RTA, CB Management Services Private Limited, into MUFG Intime India Private Limited effective May 8, 2026.
Schneider Electric Infrastructure held its Q4 FY26 earnings call on May 29, 2026, reporting FY26 order growth of 27.4%, sales growth of 9.6% and PBT growth of 10.1%, with Q4 sales flat at ₹590 Cr.

Schneider Electric Infrastructure held an earnings call on August 17, 2026, to discuss Q1FY27 results, highlighting a record order intake of ₹915 Cr and a 33% YoY growth in backlog to ₹2,100 Cr, while noting margin pressure from legacy orders and commodity inflation.
On October 18, 2026, Schneider Electric Infrastructure disclosed that the appellate authority upheld a ₹0.10 Cr transitional ITC demand and penalty for FY 2017-18.

watchlist.response: Attributed the drop to commodity costs and mix shift toward lower-margin modernization projects; said excluding commodity, margin would not have dropped.
watchlist.text: Gross margin fell from 39.1% in FY25 to 37.5% in FY26 and 36.6% in Q4; analyst asked when margin recovery would happen.

watchlist.response: Declined to give an absolute percentage, saying the dynamics keep evolving and the company is selective on profitability.
watchlist.text: Management's answers on the data-centre opportunity were seen as opaque; analyst asked for quantification.

watchlist.response: Said growth depends on customer prioritization and clearances; the company will execute orders when customers give dispatch clearance.
watchlist.text: Sales growth was single-digit in three of four quarters; analyst asked for the next growth catalyst.

watchlist.response: Price hike actions were initiated on time; margin fall is more due to operating leverage and RMI impact, which is expected to iron out.
watchlist.text: Impact of sticky commodity inflation on margins and why price hikes were not taken earlier compared to competitors.

watchlist.response: Difficult to quantify a specific number; the company is selective and strategic in engaging with contracts based on project visibility and execution ease, focusing on equipment supply and grid modernization.
watchlist.text: Visibility on the TAM for DISCOM capex and how much of it is addressable by Schneider.
